First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+2X+5 \\  & ={X}^{2}+2X+5I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}+2A+5I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & 5 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}+2A+5I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & 5 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & 5 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 & 10 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14+6+5 & 5+10+0 \\ 1+2+0 & 9+(-4)+5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}25 & 15 \\ 3 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
